_comment: Reference data for the Business impact panel. Every figure carries its
source or is labelled a hypothesis. The manual baseline is SIMULATED from
docs/BUSINESS_IMPACT.md section 2.1 until benchmark B1 (a person timing
the manual process on the same data) replaces it. CatSight's own figures
are not here: they are measured on each run.

manual_baseline.label: Simulated manual analyst - BUSINESS_IMPACT 2.1 hypothesis, to be replaced by benchmark B1
manual_baseline.reference_firm: Mid-size reinsurer, about 100 APAC cat treaties, about 25 exposed to the event

steps.step: Gather event facts (track, intensity, affected areas)

steps.catsight: Automated, a reason for every treaty
Already in the system (treaty book in Firestore)

steps.step: Estimate gross loss and apply layers

steps.catsight: Agents flag clauses; analyst reviews flagged ones only (1.5-4 h)
Analyst reviews the drafted report (2-4 h)

manual_baseline.catsight_elapsed: Same day: the automated run takes about a minute, then human review
manual_baseline.rate_note: Singapore loaded cost per analyst hour, range 70-150 (BUSINESS_IMPACT 2.2) - replace with your own

pricing.source: Vertex AI generative AI pricing (cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/pricing) - verified 2026-10-02, global endpoint; thinking tokens bill as output

jebi-2018.headline: Typhoon Jebi, 4 September 2018 - what the market actually saw

facts.text: Insured-loss estimates rose from early figures of US$3-5bn to about US$13bn - roughly three times the first view
Japanese non-life insurers paid JPY 1,067.8bn in claims (fire lines JPY 920.2bn)
facts.source: General Insurance Association of Japan (GIAJ), via BUSINESS_IMPACT B5

facts.text: Industry loss views arrived in 4-20 days (modelling firms), 6 weeks (PERILS) and up to 90 days (Verisk PCS Japan)

jebi-2018.not_like_for_like: Industry figures estimate the whole market's loss; CatSight gives a first view of one reinsurer's own book. The comparison is of speed and purpose, not of the same number.
